The State has filed this appeal under Section 378(1) & (3) of Cr.P.C. challenging the impugned judgment and order of acquittal dated 06.10.2018 passed by the I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ballari in S.C.No.10/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC r/w Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: It is the case of the prosecution that the minor victim who is the complainant was studying in SSLC in Renuka School situated at Raralu Thanda, H.B.Halli.
During the school days, she was staying with her parents.
At that time, accused used to come to her house.

It is further alleged that 5-6 months prior to the filing the complaint,
accused enticed her by giving assurance to get marry her and committed penetrative sexual assault on her many time and accused used to gave birth control tablets to the NC: 2023:KHC-D:7571-DB victim.

It is further alleged that on 24.12.2012 in the mid- night at 12.00 'O' clock, when the victim was sleeping in the house, accused came,
touched her body and committed penetrative sexual assault on her against her will and also gave life threat to her stating that if she disclose this fact to C.Ws.6 and 7, he will kill her.
It is further alleged that when the victim approached the accused to marry her, the accused refused to marry her.

Accordingly, the victim filed a complaint before H.B.Halli police station and the case was registered in crime No.18/2013 for the offences punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC r/w Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Charge was framed against the accused and he pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried.

After hearing the detailed arguments, the learned Sessions Judge formulated following points:
1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that 5 - 6 months prior to the filing of the complaint the victim / complainant during school holidays was staying in the house of her parents situated at H.B.Halli, accused came to her house and had sexual intercourse with her by giving assurance to marry her and again on 23.12.2012 in the mid-night at 12.00'o clock, when victim was sleeping in her house, accused came, touched her body and again had sexual intercourse with her and also gave birth control tablets to her thereby accused has committed an offence punishable u/S.376 of IPC?
2) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused gave life threat to the complainant victim stating that he will kill her if she disclose the said fact to CWs.6 & 7 thereby accused has committed an offence punishable u/S.506 of IPC?

After recording the evidence of the witnesses and considering the oral and documentary evidence,
the trial court answered point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative and consequently, acquitted the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
Aggrieved by the judgment of acquittal, the State has preferred this appeal.
5. We have heard the learned Additional SPP appearing for the appellant-State and learned counsel for the respondent/accused.
6. Learned Additional SPP submits that P.W.1 victim has specifically stated in her evidence that accused committed sexual assault on her against her will.

He submits that evidence of P.W.1 is corroborated by the evidence of P.Ws.3 to 5 who are the elderly persons of the village and P.W.4-mother of the victim has stated about commission of the offence by the accused and also regarding conduct of panchayath in the village.

He further submits that P.W.1 was examined on 08.10.2015 and she NC: 2023:KHC-D:7571-DB was cross-examined by the defence counsel on the same day and after lapse of one year nine months, she was again examined by the defence counsel wherein she turned hostile and deposed against her evidence as stated in her examination-in-chief.
He submits that P.Ws.3, 4 and 5 have been examined on 28.10.2015, but at that time, all these witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution.

On that day, the defence counsel has not State Of Karnataka vs Parashuram S/O Onagappa on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60417084/
3 cross-examined the witnesses, but sought time for cross- examination.
Thereafter, all these witnesses have been cross-examined on 27.06.2016 after lapse of eight months wherein the witnesses have turned hostile.
He submits that the trial court rejected the evidence of the witnesses on the ground that they have turned hostile at the time of cross-examination.

He further submits that trial court has not assigned any acceptable reasons for adjourning the case for years together and thereby not followed the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions.
He submits that P.W.7 is the Headmaster of the school and he has deposed regarding issuance of date of NC: 2023:KHC-D:7571-DB birth certificate as per ExP13.
Her date of birth is 12.06.1997 and as on the date of the incident, her age is 15 years and same has not been disputed by the defence and not cross-examined this witness.
He also submits that P.W.6 is the doctor who has examined the victim on 31.01.2013 and on examination she noticed rapture of hymen and issue medical certificate as per Ex.P7.
The evidence of all these witnesses has not been properly appreciated and thereby the trial court erred in acquitting the accused.

Hence, on these grounds he prays to allow the appeal.
7.

Per contra, learned counsel for the accused submits that P.W.1 victim herself has admitted in the cross-examination that accused not at all committed sexual assault on her nor gave life threat to her.
She has also admitted that she has not filed any complaint alleging that accused committed penetrative sexual assault on her.

She has stated that she did not produce any articles before the police nor police seized them under panchanama nor drawn panchanama.
He further submits that victim after attaining the age of majority married the accused.
He further submits that, P.W.4 mother of the victim has also admitted the fact that accused has not at all committed any of the offence alleged against him.

He submits that P.W.2 is the pencha witness in his examination-in-chief he supported the case of the prosecution, but in the cross-examination he supported the case of the defence that no panchanama was drawn in his presence as per Ex.P2 nor seized M.Os.1 to 3 in his presence.
He submits that trial court appreciating the oral and documentary evidence acquitted the accused.
The trial court was justified in passing the judgment of acquittal.
Hence, on these grounds he prays to dismiss the appeal.
